spec.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket_model}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "computed_metrics")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.cadence == "1d")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "min_outdoor_temp_c" or r._field == "avg_outdoor_temp_c" or r._field == "max_outdoor_temp_c")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then (r._value * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0 else r._value }))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_field"])
  |> group(columns: ["_field"])

from(bucket: "${bucket_raw}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "weather")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "outdoor_temp_c")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      r with
      _field: "weather_outdoor_temp_c",
      _value: if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then (r._value * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0 else r._value
  }))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_field"])

from(bucket: "${bucket_raw}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "current_temp_c")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      r with
      _field: "current_temperature",
      _value: if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then (r._value * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0 else r._value
  }))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_field"])

spec.description: This panel provides a comprehensive overview of temperature dynamics. It plots the daily computed outdoor temperature range (minimum, average, and maximum) as distinct series. Overlaid on this is the high-resolution current indoor temperature from the primary thermostat and the raw outdoor temperature from the weather feed. This combined view is essential for correlating indoor temperature fluctuations with both the broader daily outdoor trends and immediate weather changes.
spec.title: Temperature Overview: Outdoor Daily Range + Indoor/Outdoor Live

spec.description: This panel visualizes the thermal performance of the structure by plotting individual thermal resistance (R-Factor) calculations against the temperature difference (ΔT) between inside and outside. Each point represents a single heating or cooling cycle transition. The chart separates observations for heating (positive ΔT) and cooling (negative ΔT) and calculates a running median baseline for each mode. This helps identify the building's effective insulation performance under different thermal load conditions.
spec.title: R-Factor

spec.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket_raw}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "indoor_dynamics")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) =>
      r._field == "thermal_recovery_ratio" or
      r._field == "indoor_temp_c" or
      r._field == "outdoor_temp_c"
  )
  |> pivot(rowKey:["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.thermal_recovery_ratio and exists r.indoor_temp_c and exists r.outdoor_temp_c)
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      delta_c = r.indoor_temp_c - r.outdoor_temp_c
      abs_delta_c = if delta_c < 0.0 then -delta_c else delta_c

      // Recover physical temperature change rate (°C/hr)
      raw_rate_c = r.thermal_recovery_ratio * abs_delta_c

      // Dynamically scale both axes according to the dashboard unit toggle
      delta_scaled = if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then delta_c * 1.8 else delta_c
      rate_scaled = if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then raw_rate_c * 1.8 else raw_rate_c

      return {
          _time: r._time,
          dev_idx: r.dev_idx,
          raw_rate_c: raw_rate_c,
          delta_t: delta_scaled,
          recovery_rate: rate_scaled
      }
  })
  // Filter out standby zero-drift noise and physically impossible short-cycle spikes (> 4.5 °C/hr = ~8.1 °F/hr)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.raw_rate_c > 0.05 and r.raw_rate_c < 4.5)
  |> drop(columns: ["raw_rate_c"])
  |> group(columns: ["dev_idx"])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])

spec.description: This panel analyzes the HVAC system's efficiency by plotting the Thermal Recovery Rate (the speed at which the system changes the indoor temperature, in °/hour) against the Indoor-Outdoor temperature delta (ΔT). Each point represents a completed HVAC cycle. The chart fits an independent linear regression model for each selected device, providing a clear trendline of how the system's heating/cooling power changes as the outdoor temperature difference increases. This is a key indicator of HVAC performance and duct efficiency.
spec.title: Thermal Recovery Ratio

spec.query:
import "date"

// 1. Fetch daily average outdoor temperature
temps = from(bucket: "${bucket_model}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "computed_metrics")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.cadence == "1d")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "avg_outdoor_temp_c")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then (r._value * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0 else r._value }))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _time: date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1d) }))

// 2. Fetch daily runtimes for every independent operational stage
runtimes = from(bucket: "${bucket_model}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "computed_metrics")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.cadence == "1d")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => 
      r._field == "heating_stage1_time" or
      r._field == "heating_stage2_time" or
      r._field == "cooling_stage1_time" or
      r._field == "cooling_stage2_time" or
      r._field == "alt_heat_stage1_time" or
      r._field == "alt_heat_stage2_time"
  )
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value / 3600.0 }))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _time: date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1d) }))

// 3. Interleave and pivot side-by-side
union(tables: [temps, runtimes])
  |> group(columns: ["_time", "dev_idx", "_field"])
  |> last()
  |> group(columns: ["dev_idx"])
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.avg_outdoor_temp_c)
  
  // 4. THERMODYNAMIC SANITIZATION: Nullify cross-seasonal leakage before Plotly regression runs (Table data must have 0s instead of NULLs for trendline regression)
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      // If its colder than 65°F (or 18.3°C), strip out phantom cooling runtime data
      is_cold = if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then r.avg_outdoor_temp_c < 50.0 else r.avg_outdoor_temp_c < 10
      is_hot = if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then r.avg_outdoor_temp_c > 75.0 else r.avg_outdoor_temp_c > 24
      
      return {
        r with
        cooling_stage1_time: if is_cold then 0.0 else r.cooling_stage1_time,
        cooling_stage2_time: if is_cold then 0.0 else r.cooling_stage2_time,
        // Conversely, nullify heating triggers during warm periods if necessary
        heating_stage1_time: if is_hot then 0.0 else r.heating_stage1_time,
        heating_stage2_time: if is_hot then 0.0 else r.heating_stage2_time,
        alt_heat_stage1_time: if is_hot then 0.0 else r.alt_heat_stage1_time,
        alt_heat_stage2_time: if is_hot then 0.0 else r.alt_heat_stage2_time
      }
  })
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])

spec.description: This panel plots the daily runtime of each HVAC stage against the average outdoor temperature for that day. Each point represents a single day's performance. A linear regression trendline is fitted for each stage, which helps visualize how runtime demand for heating and cooling scales with outdoor temperature. This is useful for identifying the outdoor temperature crossover points where the system switches from heating to cooling and for assessing the load-dependency of each stage.
spec.title: Daily Runtime vs. Outdoor Temperature

spec.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket_model}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "computed_metrics")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.cadence == "1d")
  |> filter(fn: (r) =>
      r._field == "heating_stage1_time" or
      r._field == "heating_stage2_time" or
      r._field == "alt_heat_stage1_time" or
      r._field == "alt_heat_stage2_time" or
      r._field == "cooling_stage1_time" or
      r._field == "cooling_stage2_time" or
      r._field == "fan_time" or
      r._field == "total_humidifier_time")
  // Convert from seconds to hours instantly
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value / 3600.0 }))
  
  // Drop raw rows that are 0 or negative before grouping/pivoting
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._value > 0.0)
  
  |> group(columns: ["_time"])
  
  // Pivot only the surviving dates that actually have data
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  
  |> filter(fn: (r) => 
      exists r.heating_stage1_time or 
      exists r.heating_stage2_time or 
      exists r.alt_heat_stage1_time or 
      exists r.alt_heat_stage2_time or 
      exists r.cooling_stage1_time or 
      exists r.cooling_stage2_time or 
      exists r.fan_time or 
      exists r.total_humidifier_time
  )
  // Dynamically calculate pure independent Fan-Only circulation runtime.
  // Nest energizes G (fan) during cooling, heat pump (h1/h2), and humidification,
  // but NOT during furnace-controlled alt heat (ah1/ah2).
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      h1 = if exists r.heating_stage1_time then r.heating_stage1_time else 0.0
      h2 = if exists r.heating_stage2_time then r.heating_stage2_time else 0.0
      c1 = if exists r.cooling_stage1_time then r.cooling_stage1_time else 0.0
      c2 = if exists r.cooling_stage2_time then r.cooling_stage2_time else 0.0
      hum = if exists r.total_humidifier_time then r.total_humidifier_time else 0.0
      
      fan_coupled = h1 + h2 + c1 + c2 + hum
      raw_fan = if exists r.fan_time then r.fan_time else 0.0
      
      fan_only = if raw_fan > fan_coupled then raw_fan - fan_coupled else 0.0

      return {
        _time: r._time,
        heating_stage1_time: r.heating_stage1_time,
        heating_stage2_time: r.heating_stage2_time,
        alt_heat_stage1_time: r.alt_heat_stage1_time,
        alt_heat_stage2_time: r.alt_heat_stage2_time,
        cooling_stage1_time: r.cooling_stage1_time,
        cooling_stage2_time: r.cooling_stage2_time,
        humidifier_time: r.total_humidifier_time,
        fan_time: fan_only
      }
  })
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])

spec.description: This chart displays a detailed breakdown of the total daily runtime (in hours) for each individual HVAC operational stage. This includes primary heating/cooling stages (1 and 2), alternate/auxiliary heat stages, independent fan-only circulation (calculated by subtracting HVAC-driven fan time from total fan time), and humidifier runtime. The stacked bar format provides a clear view of total system activity and the contribution of each component on any given day.
spec.title: Daily HVAC Runtime by Stage (Hours)

spec.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket_model}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "computed_metrics")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.cadence == "1d")
  |> filter(fn: (r) =>
      r._field == "total_heat_time" or
      r._field == "total_alt_heat_time" or
      r._field == "total_cooling_time" or
      r._field == "fan_time" or
      r._field == "total_humidifier_time")
  // 1. Convert from raw seconds to hours immediately
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value / 3600.0 }))
  
  // 2. Group by time to line up all fields for the same calendar day
  |> group(columns: ["_time"])
  
  // 3. Pivot early so we can safely do cross-field calculations
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  
  // 4. Strip fan-coupled runtimes (heat pump, cooling, humidifier) to isolate pure FAN-only runtime
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      hc = if exists r.total_heat_time then r.total_heat_time else 0.0
      cc = if exists r.total_cooling_time then r.total_cooling_time else 0.0
      hum = if exists r.total_humidifier_time then r.total_humidifier_time else 0.0
      
      fan_coupled = hc + cc + hum
      raw_fan = if exists r.fan_time then r.fan_time else 0.0
      
      fan_only = if raw_fan > fan_coupled then raw_fan - fan_coupled else 0.0

      return {
        _time: r._time,
        total_heat_time: r.total_heat_time,
        total_alt_heat_time: r.total_alt_heat_time,
        total_cooling_time: r.total_cooling_time,
        total_humidifier_time: r.total_humidifier_time,
        fan_time: fan_only
      }
  })
  
  // 5. Merge streams into a single clean data frame for Grafana's stacking engine
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])

spec.description: This panel provides a high-level summary of daily HVAC usage by aggregating runtimes into total heating, total cooling, total alternate heat, and independent fan circulation. This is useful for understanding the primary mode of HVAC operation each day and comparing the energy mix at a glance. Runtimes are shown in hours.

  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)

spec.description: This chart shows the relative percentage of time each HVAC stage was active during a day's total runtime. It helps visualize the system's reliance on higher stages (e.g., Stage 2 heating/cooling) versus lower, more efficient stages. A day with a high percentage of Stage 2 usage indicates a higher thermal load that the primary stage could not handle alone.
spec.title: Daily Stage Mix (Percentage)

spec.description: This panel displays the total number of on/off cycles per day for each primary HVAC mode: heating, cooling, fan, and humidifier. The 'Fan' cycle count is specifically calculated to represent only the cycles where the fan ran independently, excluding cycles where it ran as part of a heating or cooling call. This helps in diagnosing equipment short-cycling and understanding system usage patterns.
spec.title: Daily Cycle Counts by Mode

spec.query:
// 1. Load the base data once to be efficient
  base_data = from(bucket: "${bucket_raw}")
    |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "indoor_dynamics")
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dev_idx =~ /${device:regex}/)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field =~ /^delta_deg_c_per_hr_.*/ or r._field == "outdoor_temp_c")

  // 2. Create a stream of only the delta fields
  deltas = base_data
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field =~ /^delta_deg_c_per_hr_.*/)

  // 3. Create a stream of only the temperature, renaming value to avoid collision
  temps = base_data
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "outdoor_temp_c")
    |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with temp_val: r._value }))
    |> drop(columns: ["_field", "_value"])

  // 4. Join the streams on time and device index
  enriched = join(tables: {d: deltas, t: temps}, on: ["_time", "dev_idx"])
      |> drop(columns: ["t"]) // Clean up the joined table structure

  // 5. Transform records into individual observation objects
  transformed = enriched
    |> map(fn: (r) => ({
        _time: r._time,
        _dev_idx: r.dev_idx, // Keep as original type for the grouping/accumulator
        x: if "${temp_unit}" == "F" then (r.temp_val * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0 else r.temp_val,
        y: r._value,
        stage: r._field
    }))
    |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.x and exists r.y and r.y != 0.0)
    // Group by dev_idx so reduce runs once per device
    |> group(columns: ["dev_idx"])


  transformed

spec.description: This scatter plot shows the relationship between the HVAC system's performance (rate of temperature change in °/hr) and the outdoor temperature at the time of the cycle. Each point represents a single HVAC cycle, colored by its operational stage (e.g., Heat S1, Cool S2). A smoothed trendline (LOWESS regression) is fitted for each stage, revealing how its heating or cooling power varies with outdoor conditions. This is a powerful tool for diagnosing performance issues and understanding the system's operational envelope.
spec.title: HVAC Performance vs. Outdoor Temperature
